body: Brian Steel fans might like this week's Court of Appeals oral argument. This case is one where Steel himself was trial counsel. Billy Greg Pruitt was convicted of aggravated assault for displaying a BB gun at an off-duty police officer. Most of the oral argument is about a strong 404(b) issue: the trial court allowed evidence of a prior incident where Pruitt fired an actual gun. Allegations are not findings of guilt.

source_caption_text:
Brian Steel fans might like this week's Court of Appeals oral argument. This case is one where Steel himself was trial counsel.

Billy Greg Pruitt was convicted of aggravated assault for displaying a BB gun at an off-duty police officer. Most of the oral argument is about a strong 404(b) issue: the trial court allowed evidence of a prior incident where Pruitt fired an actual gun.

The justices seem to agree that it had little or no relevance: "Are you arguing harmless error? I'm trying to figure out why I care."

A26A2155.  BILLY GREG PRUITT v. THE STATE
